column4: Review failed open in the landing path: train.sh check set review=0 when no review command existed (no error), its review leg rejected only a published findings note (absent, malformed or blocked passed after a zero exit), and land read no review record at all, so a check run with --no-review landed like any other (facts-decision landed at ab537833d after train.sh check --no-review). Structural cause: review was enforced only as one leg's exit status inside check, a missing reviewer was mapped to a disabled leg, and land trusted CI alone: no reader of review provenance existed at land time. Fixed on wip/fix-landing-machinery (a173432e): check fails with no review command; review_provenance (verify.sh on origin's notes: a clean head note, or with no head note a clean note on every member at its exact SHA) gates both the review leg and land

column4: scripts/land/acceptance.sh's check leg ran train.sh check --no-review --no-remote, so an accepted rehearsal (the record the move gate trusts) could rest on a check that skipped review, and agents cannot run it (the permission system treats --no-review as a CI bypass); both its build leg and its broken-build control defaulted to make build, which the restarted root (no Makefile; nix develop --command lake build) does not have; its header described only --no-review and make build. column4: Sandboxes inherit the caller's git environment. scripts/checks/review_tool.sh isolated git config only, not the repository-locating variables; a pre-push hook of a LINKED worktree exports GIT_DIR=<repo>/.git/worktrees/<name>, so every git -C <sandbox> in the check acted on the caller. On 2026-11-06 `train.sh ci laudit` run from the linked worktree ~agent/audit-records made the hook's review_tool.sh create its test branches (nonff, capped, parse-*) and set core.bare=true in ~agent/audit-clone (kept unchanged as evidence), and push 28 commits to origin refs/notes/concrete-review (tip b4b364f4, pre-leak 5b6add0d) and 12 to refs/notes/concrete-review-findings (tip 21c56796, pre-leak fd3c6451), authored Review Gate, 17:16:49-17:17:43Z, annotating 21 sandbox commits that exist on no remote (first counted as 22, which wrongly included c54679c3, a real commit whose note at 17:21Z is legitimate); no earlier note was deleted or changed and every reader looks notes up by exact SHA, so none can count as provenance for a real commit. lambdaclass has no notes refs. Codex confirmed with a bounded reproducer on concrete-ci-2 at main f9a8c333 (caller refs and refs/notes/* changed: LEAK) and an independent GIT_DIR experiment. landing_script.sh and landing_bot.sh unset only five of git's local variables; legacy_frozen.sh, acceptance.sh, run-at-ref.sh and bot.sh unset none. Second incident, same cause: the first reproducer installed a pre-push hook that ran review_tool.sh; the leaked GIT_DIR made each nested push re-enter that hook, the recursion exhausted fede-256gb (load ~1900) and the OOM killer took down the orchestrator's session. Structural owner: the sandbox helper scripts/checks/lib/git_sandbox.sh (unsets every `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` variable), sourced by every repository-making script; reproducers and tests run with no installed hook, under timeout 120 and a 512-task / 8G systemd scope bound, or a finite cgroup memory.max plus a process limit, and never an unbounded run. Closed 2026-11-07: the fix landed at dbe838488891, where every closure part is checked in Root checks (scripts/checks/run.sh, all 11 pass: sandbox_isolation PASS=13 FAIL=0 with its structural leg over 9 scripts, the two live linked-worktree probes and the leaking control; landing_script PASS=208 FAIL=0 with the linked-worktree, hook-off, foreign-hook and identify refusal legs; also run on concrete-ci-2 at 8e62e377) (train siso from a full clone; reviewed by Codex, rounds clean at 8e62e377, and Kimi; CI run 42424663064; main CI 42425007584 on origin and 42425010605 on lambdaclass, both success). The stray notes were removed from origin by one forward fast-forward commit per ref on its then-current tip, no force: refs/notes/concrete-review d4bdcae22d50 -> dcffeea8e6cd (21 entries removed, 224 untouched at the push; Codex confirmed the list against the earlier tip 8cbb7db253f7, where 223 were untouched, and the one commit between that tip and d4bdcae22d50 only added a legitimate note for 9d6dc01a, so the removal list is identical) and refs/notes/concrete-review-findings 301e929e1bab -> 5d7c6dc3dad5 (11 removed, 105 untouched); the 40 leaked commits wrote 33 entries, one of which they removed themselves (0c04c01c); Codex confirmed the removal list and the tree diffs before the push; lambdaclass has no notes refs and none were created. ~agent/audit-clone is kept unchanged as evidence with LEAK-EVIDENCE-README.txt

column4: CI run 42424028055 (train legacydocs at 4d0355a56e, a docs-only change over 93850111) failed Kernel replay (leanchecker): the per-module leg replayed ConcreteSpec.Spec.Ownership, a module renamed to Slice1Ownership by 44ee1231, and stopped on unknown constant 'ConcreteSpec.lookupF'. The job's lake cache had been restored through a restore-key prefix from the cache of train commit 5b894432ad, whose sources predate the rename. Non-fresh `leanchecker ConcreteSpec` picks every .olean on the search path whose name has the prefix (the toolchain's LeanChecker.lean, lines 91-94), so orphaned build files are replayed. Reproducer: build 44ee1231^, build 93850111's sources over that build directory, run scripts/proofs/kernel_replay.sh: FAIL on the Checker/Syntax orphans; a clean build of the same sources passes. Codex confirmed it with that reproducer (2026-11-07). Structural cause: the replay took its module list from the build directory's contents instead of the sources.

Validation on the working-tree patch over b64725db00d409f387fcb90b71ef659b1f0bdfbc under nix develop -c: review_tool 140/0, landing_ready 14/0, landing_script 279/0, sandbox_isolation 15/0, issues 5/0, doc_links 12/0 (pass/fail). Round 3 repair: schema-first complete history scan preserves maximum rounds across merge parents and unresolved findings until a covering descendant review; insufficient scope forces full review, valid blocked scope does not emit a false diagnostic. Explicit --notes-ref replaces ambient ref selection; readiness rejects explicit empty bases. Updated controls run against the prior implementation reproduce cap, findings, blocked-round and argument/ref failures. Round 3 validation on working-tree patch over 2b4b3d9a700880384099e2e6019bad85b5077514 under nix develop -c with bounded_run 120: review_tool 156/0, landing_ready 19/0, landing_script 279/0, sandbox_isolation 15/0, issues 5/0, doc_links 12/0 (pass/fail). Round 4 repair: shared verify.sh remains the single schema/range authority for all consumers; incremental topological scan discards insufficient scope only when a completed covering descendant supersedes it, retaining maximum rounds and uncovered merge-side evidence. Mode-specific commit messages prevent same-second fixture collisions; reviewer call/file assertions and positive delta hunks prevent vacuous negative controls. Recovery controls pin clean-at-cap and findings shortcuts, resumed delta scope, and uncovered merge siblings. Round 4 validation on working-tree patch over 41b8c5f8b8b61f5281a242400b7a0de6d77a6a90 under nix develop -c with bounded_run 120: review_tool 179/0 (fixed Git timestamps), landing_ready 19/0, landing_script 279/0, sandbox_isolation 15/0, issues 5/0, doc_links 12/0 (pass/fail), no incomplete runs. Bounded 120-second baseline controls reproduce readiness and incremental bypasses and signoff record/verify/train acceptance; direct argument/non-ancestor/shallow controls pin existing fail-closed verifier behavior.
